question: Which Windows power mode (performance power slider overlay) is active?
reason: Microsoft documents the power mode (performance power slider) overlays and their GUIDs (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/customize-power-slider) and that "powercfg /q" without arguments enumerates the active overlay scheme when one is active (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options), but no command that prints the active overlay by itself; the decoder compares the scheme GUID printed by /query (power_settings) with /getactivescheme (power_active_scheme) and names a documented overlay GUID when they differ, which is an interpretation of that sentence, not a direct read

documented_paths.why_not_used: read by the power_settings source; Microsoft says it enumerates the active overlay when one is active, so the decoder derives the overlay from the GUID it prints, which is marked as derived
documents the overlay GUIDs, not a command that prints the active one

follow_up: a documented direct read of the active overlay, if Microsoft publishes one
